decision.question: Which onboarding change should be reverted or tested first to recover trial activation?

affected.who: New trial accounts in their first 7 days
affected.process: Onboarding: welcome email and first workspace

problem_statement: Trial activation fell after two onboarding changes shipped days apart; the export shows both conditions associated with lower activation but cannot separate their effects.

statements.text: 31 percent of September 2026 trials activated within 7 days.
Trials with a welcome email delayed more than 24 hours activated at 20 percent versus 37.6 percent for the rest.
Trials created without sample data activated at 23 percent versus 39 percent with sample data.
Trials with both conditions activated at 15 percent.
The email batch change (2026-08-28) and opt-in sample data (2026-09-01) shipped four days apart.
The nightly email batch delays the first-step guide and lowers activation.
An empty workspace without sample data stalls first project creation and lowers activation.
Trial sign-up mix did not change between August and September.
The separate causal effect of each change is unknown.
statements.resolution: Run a two-by-two staggered rollback (immediate email, default sample data) with random assignment for 14 days.

alternatives.summary: Revert the welcome email to immediate send first.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cheap to revert; if sample data is the main driver, activation barely moves.
Addresses the larger observed gap; touches first-run experience design.

alternatives.summary: Randomized two-by-two rollback of both changes for 14 days.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Separates the effects and their interaction; needs enough trials per cell and a short delay.

next_action.action: Design the randomized two-by-two rollback, with per-cell sample size computed from the 800-trial September volume, before reverting either change.

nodes.test: Randomize immediate versus batched welcome email; if activation does not differ, reject.
Randomize default versus opt-in sample data; if first-project creation does not differ, reject.

why_tree.stop_reason: Each branch reaches a testable hypothesis; the export is observational, so further whys would be speculation.

partition.criterion: Onboarding step where the trial stalls: communication (welcome email) versus first-use content (sample data).
partition.overlaps: Trials with both conditions belong to both branches.
partition.omitted: Sign-up mix changes and seasonality (recorded as an assumption).
partition.interaction_assessment: Both-condition trials activated at 15 percent, below either condition alone, so the effects may compound; because the changes shipped four days apart, only random assignment can estimate each effect and their interaction.
